PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The proposed project is a request for the continued operation of an existing major wireless
telecommunications facility located at 42035 20th Street East for a period of 10 years.
The facility was previously approved as an 80-foot-high monopole and a 192 square foot
equipment enclosure with a 1,900 square foot lease area. The existing facility consists of
20 panel antennas mounted on an 80-foot monopole with eight Remote Radio Units
(RRUs), one dish antenna, four cabinets, one generator, one concrete masonry unit
(CMU) equipment enclosure, and a chain link fence surrounding an approximately 890
square foot lease area at the subject site. The applicant is not proposing to expand the
lease area. The current carriers at the existing facility are Verizon Wireless and T-Mobile.

BACKGROUND

On January 14, 2010, the Planning Commission approved CUP 09-026 (Resolution No.
PC-2010-004), which allowed for the construction of an 80-foot-high major wireless
telecommunications facility and a 192 square foot equipment enclosure. On
November 9, 2022, Dish Wireless submitted a Minor Modification application to the
Planning Division for a collocation; however, CUP 09-026 expired on January 26, 2020.
On January 17, 2023, Crown Castle USA LLC submitted an application for a Time
Extension (CUP 09-026TE) to the original CUP. Subsequently, staff deemed the
application incomplete and directed the applicant to submit a new CUP application since
CUP 09-026 was expired.

Pursuant to Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC) Section 17.95.040.A, wireless
telecommunications facilities expire after a period of 10 years, unless a time extension is
approved. Since a time extension application was not received by the Planning Division
prior to expiration of the facility, the entitlement expired, and a new CUP is required for
the continued operation of the facility.

The project site contains 25 western Joshua Trees, grasses, and minimal brush; however,
the applicant has not proposed to expand the lease area of the existing major wireless
telecommunications facility. The southern most portion of the site contains the existing
Southern California Edison substation and is vegetated with a combination of weeds and
desert scrub.

The existing facility has been modified since original approval through the following Minor
Modifications (MM):

    MM 13-049 approved on August 20, 2013;
    MM 14-001 approved on January 1, 2014; and,
    MM 15-002 approved on January 8, 2015.

At the time of approval of the original CUP, the project was subject to the Industrial
General Plan Land Use designation and the M-2 (General Industrial) zone. The maximum
height for the zone was 45 feet allowing up to 65 feet with approval of a CUP. The
Planning Commission made findings to allow for additional 15 feet of height in order to
provide adequate service in the area. Since the expiration of the original CUP, the General
Plan Land Use designation and zone have changed to IND (Industrial) and U (Utilities)
respectively. Per PMC Section 17.73.010, Wireless telecommunications facilities are not
permitted in the U zone; however, the applicant is not proposing to expand the lease area
or increase the height of the existing monopole.

The subject application was initially submitted on May 24, 2023. After resolution of
completeness items, the application was deemed complete on July 24, 2023, and
scheduled for the September 14, 2023, Planning Commission hearing.

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), an Initial Study was
prepared for the project in conjunction with the original approval and on January 14, 2010,
the Planning Commission adopted a Mitigated Negative Declaration (MND) finding that,
with the incorporation of mitigation measures, the project would not have a significant
impact on the environment. Staff has reviewed the MND and Mitigation Monitoring and
Reporting Program (MMRP) to determine whether the project triggered any of the
conditions described in Sections 15162, 15163, and 15164 of the CEQA Guidelines and
determined that additional documentation is not required for the project because
CUP 23-009 does not propose any significant revisions to the project, there are no
changes in circumstances and there is no new information of substantial importance that
will involve new significant environmental effects or increase the severity of previously
identified significant effects. As previously mentioned, the project site contains 25 western
Joshua Trees, grasses and minimal brush; however, the applicant has not proposed to
expand the existing facility. The proposed project is a request to continue the operation
of an existing major wireless telecommunications facility and does not include any
alterations to the major wireless telecommunications facility as approved through
CUP 09-026. Furthermore, a Radio Frequency report was submitted as part of the
mitigation monitoring program and shows that the project will continue to be compliant
with Federal Communications Commission rules and regulations, as described in the
Office of Engineering and Technology Bulletin 65.

1.  Adopt Resolution No. PC-2023-020 approving CUP 23-009 and find that the
  project is consistent with the previously adopted MND and MMRP.

2.  Continue the project and direct staff to return with additional information.

3.  Deny the project.

Option 1 is recommended.

There are three wireless communications sources that generate and use

Electromagnetic energy exists in a variety of forms, including radio and
television waves, microwaves, heat lamp radiation, visible and ultraviolet
light, and electrical currents passing through wires.  Whenever
electromagnetic energy moves from one point to another through electrical
wires, the movement is accompanied by the formation of electric and
magnetic fields (also referred to as electromagnetic fields, or EMFs).
Whenever electromagnetic energy moves from one point to another by
waves propagated through space, the movement is accompanied by the
formation or radiofrequency radiation (RFR).

EMFs have been the subject of recent scientific and public interest
because of some epidemiological studies suggesting a link between EMF
exposures and certain types of health concerns. Health concerns about
EMFs have centered around high-power electrical sources, such as high-
voltage electrical transmission lines. However, the EMFs associated with
electrical equipment used in wireless communications systems such as
pumps, motors, switches, and telephones are relatively low intensity and
generally not considered a health problem.

All forms of transmitted electromagnetic energy travel at the speed of light.
Depending on how it was generated and transmitted, radiofrequency
radiation (RFR) will radiate outward from the source in energy packets that
have the characteristics of waves, particles, or a combination of both.
Once generated, these waves of energy travel from their transmitter
through space to their receiver, where they are reflected from, refracted
around, or absorbed by it. It is the absorbed energy which is the source of
health-related concerns. However, wireless communications systems
generally use lower frequencies and lower energy levels than are

absorbed at all, this type of energy is absorbed as heat. Unless generated

are almost always too low to affect biological materials.

Non-ionizing radiation is not known to damage DNA as can ionizing

molecule short, linear groups of atoms extend off of a main chain or body

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The proposed project is a request for the continued operation of an existing major wireless
communication facility located at 906 East Avenue R. The facility was previously
approved by CUP 11-007 for a 75-foot monopole tower with antennas and associated
ground equipment within a 912 square foot, six-foot wall and with a wrought iron fence
entryway. The site is within an existing towing service and storage facility consisting of 15
acres. The major telecommunication facility, and enclosure, are located at the southeast
corner of the site.

On November 10, 2011, the Planning Commission approved CUP 11-007 (Resolution
No. PC-2011-048), which allowed for the construction of a 75-foot-high major wireless
telecommunication facility and 912 square foot enclosure. CUP 11-007 expired on
November 28, 2021

Pursuant to Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC) Section 17.95.040.A, wireless
telecommunication facilities expire after 10 years, unless a time extension application is
approved. Since a time extension application was not received by the Planning Division
prior to the expiration of the facility, the entitlement expired, and a new CUP is required
for the continued operation of the facility.
